fills.researcher_notes: Could not find a sourced commissioning year for this specific internal 41 km/40in gas line between fields 103D and 103A (both in Zueitina Oil Co's Sirte-basin concession 103). What IS established: field 103 (Intisar/Idris) was discovered by Occidental in late 1967, with a 40-inch OIL export pipeline to Zueitina terminal built/operating by February 1968 (AAPG Explorer 'The Oil Hunters of Libya', verified live; OSTI biblio/6090661 on Occidental's Libyan gas-reinjection operations, verified/fetched). Critically, that OSTI paper describes the ORIGINAL 1968-era design as reinjecting associated gas back into the reservoir for pressure maintenance rather than piping it to shore -- meaning the gas-gathering pipelines (like this 103D-103A line) were very likely a later addition once gas began being piped/sold rather than reinjected, not contemporaneous with the 1968 oil buildout. Per the protocol, a field's first-production year is not automatically its pipeline's commissioning year, and I am treating the 1968 date as exactly that kind of non-answer -- flagging it, not using it. The only firm anchor I have is a upper bound: OPEC ASB Table 4.10 (2011 data, recovered from Wayback + pdftotext per the protocol's known gotcha) already lists '103D/103A, Zueitina, ...' as an existing, operating, capacity-reporting line in 2011, so it was commissioned no later than 2011. No dated news article, company history, or trade-press piece naming an actual construction/commissioning year for this specific segment turned up before the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted. Marking UNRESOLVED rather than guessing.

MEED (2005 construction-tender article, verified live) describes 'Zueitina's 103A supply base in the Sirte basin', confirming Zueitina Oil Co as the operator of the field-103/103A infrastructure this internal gas line sits within, consistent with the sheet's existing (currently unreferenced) Operator value. Tier medium rather than high: this MEED mention is about the broader Field-103A supply-base project, not a citation naming the specific 103D-103A segment by name, and I could not find a second, fully independent source that names this exact 41 km internal line. OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 also lists '103D/103A' under owner/operator 'Zueitina' (same recovered-PDF source used for the length observation below), but I am not double-counting it as a second independent source here since it is the same underlying document family already cited for P1856/the length flag on this cluster.

validity.recommendation: Not flagged in this brief (no length_ratio flag was raised for P1857), so not proposing a fill -- but flagging for a human to check separately: OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (recovered via Wayback + pdftotext, see P1856's shard for the full unit-mislabeling explanation) lists '103D/103A, Zueitina, 26, 40in, 17,841,971' where the raw '26' is very likely already in km (not miles, despite the column header) -- cross-checked against ASB2013's re-statement of the same route as '16.12' mi, and 16.12 x 1.609 = 25.9 km, matching ASB2012's raw 26 almost exactly. That would make the true length ~26 km, not the sheet's current 41.00 km (41.00 = 26 x 1.609, i.e. the same double-conversion bug identified on P1856's 333 km).
